title: Injured in the Cabin in the Sky fight scene and the retake dispute
summary: Rochester's shove knocks him out on the table; he is patched up quickly and refuses a retake without a contract until he relents.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: jealous. So we get together dancing. So Rochester gets mad because we're dancing and he wants to come over and stop me from dancing with Ethel. So we start a fight. He shoves me over a table, course it was all set to do, but he did it, seemingly overdid it. He shoved me too hard, they got me to the table sooner than I expected to be, made me hit the table wrongly on the top of my spine, which knocked me cold. So I'm on the floor but I'm out and don't know it but I'm still going through the motions. So I take my feet up and he comes and gets on my feet, I have my feet on his chest and I shove him and in shoving him I shoved him with double the strangth I would have had seemingly off of me and shoved him off of his pad he's going to fall on and the Director says "cut." When he said "cut" they got me up off the floor, took me to the bar to rest a while, but I couldn't go no further. But they were surprised that I carried that film to a cut from where it was, I fought the scene out to a cut, you know what I

mean? It's good the Director said "Cut" at the time he did 'cause I couldn't play good no further. So anyway they took me to the hospital, took me over to a room on the lot where there's a first aid kit and got me together good as they could and then I wound up in the hospital; and it was about four or five days before I could get out of the hospital, and then they got with the doctor and told him to patch me up that I got to have him finish the film and they won't let me finish the film because in the contract, everybody is under contract so the longer they have to wait the more they have to pay the people. So they wanted to get rid of me right quick. So they bandaged me up and got me out quick, to get me back over and now they call it retake, but the part they're going to take I have never done before. So I refused to do the retake idea they had being out from the contract. Put me back on the contract and I'll do the retake. But don't take me out from the contract and

do a retaking and I'm not doing something I haven't done before. So it held up the play about maybe an hour until I decided that I would go ahead and do this, what's it going to mean anyway. So I did the part anyway and they found out I was doing the part and everybody subsided to the point where they were not anxious to get this fella here to, you know, to get me going because they got me going, because I did it on my own, but I didn't get anything for it, no credit, nothing. I haven't played the picture since for them.

But however, they knew how I felt about it. I wasn't going to jump to it, I just did it on good graces to cut down the expenses of the cameramen and all the people who had to stay there that were on the contract regardless of the play. They gotta work, too, you know. So I got that out of the way. And that was the end of that one.
